notes: One attack.py pipeline must, for any relay directory: recognise the exact 'encoded_<base64url unpadded>' naming convention (and not be fooled by look-alike decoys), recover original filenames (restoring base64url padding), decrypt each node body (standard base64 then byte-wise XOR with the repeated password key, validating UTF-8), emit name/plaintext artifacts in sorted order, and extract the single normalized secret word from the VAULT-VERDICT line. The debugging/ambiguity and adversary scores come from the unpadded-base64url restoration, the XOR/key-repetition decoding, mandatory skip of malformed and non-UTF-8 nodes, and the exact case/hyphen/digit normalization of the secret token. Hidden generalization comes from three genuinely different relay trees (fresh set, adversarial decoy set incl. a convention-matching but non-UTF-8 node, and an edge set with hyphen/dot/long unpadded names) that the deliverable must pass via the same CLI interface. Dropped the hard-floor reverse-engineered radix/range decoder competency (C-e41d6ebb) to keep the task coherent at the medium target.
